complexity.notes: The lower() call copies the whole string, costing O(n) space; lowercasing each character at comparison time (s[a].lower() != s[b].lower()) would make the algorithm O(1) space. The early return inside the left-skip loop is correct but reads awkwardly; checking a pointer crossover after both skips would be tidier. Behavior matches for the full printable-ASCII set since isalnum() agrees with the problem's alphanumeric definition there.
complexity.summary: Lowercases the string, then moves two pointers inward from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and returning False on the first mismatch. The inner skip on the left index bails out with True if it runs off the end, covering all-non-alphanumeric input.
